title: Why Is My Home Wi-Fi Slow?

seo.title: Why Is My Home Wi-Fi Slow?
seo.meta_description: Slow Wi-Fi can come from the internet connection, distance from the router, interference, too many devices, or aging equipment.
seo.search_intent: Identify the likely causes of “why is my home wi-fi slow,” use observable clues to decide what to check first, and know when the problem is no longer basic household troubleshooting.

excerpt: Slow Wi-Fi can come from the internet connection, distance from the router, interference, too many devices, or aging equipment. First separate a Wi-Fi problem from an internet-service problem.
content_html:
Slow Wi-Fi can come from the internet connection, distance from the router, interference, too many devices, or aging equipment. First separate a Wi-Fi problem from an internet-service problem.

Compare wired and Wi-Fi performance if possible

If a wired device is also slow, the bottleneck may be the ISP, modem, or service plan. If only Wi-Fi is affected, focus on coverage and interference.

Test near and far from the router

A large improvement near the router points to coverage. Dense walls, metal, large objects, and multiple floors can weaken the signal.

Check whether slowness is time-dependent

Backups, streaming, game downloads, and video calls can saturate the connection. If every device slows at once, look for shared traffic.

Restart methodically and update

Restarting the modem and router can clear temporary faults, but it will not fix poor coverage. Keep firmware updated and consider repositioning or replacing obsolete equipment if the pattern persists.
